item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract: it exposes the exact Upload signature, buffers a replayable multipart body, preserves Add, and explicitly tests source-reader errors. Both patches violate scope and fail to route Upload through Add, but A adds substantially more forbidden API and retry machinery.","reasons":["B matches the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A substitutes ...UploadFileOption.","B covers multipart field/name/content, retry with streamed os.File content, validation before requests, and source-reader errors. A lacks the required source-reader-error test.","A changes RawClient request-body ownership and replay behavior globally via makeBodyReplayable, despite the contract explicitly forbidding unrelated retry refactoring.","A changes the return types of WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions and introduces multiple option interfaces, creating unnecessary API churn around an otherwise small convenience method."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's request, decoding, and error path.","Adds association fields and a raw WithFileFormValue option, explicitly contrary to the contract.","Expands multipartbody with NewFileWithFields instead of simply using the established NewFile helper as requested, and changes global seekable-reader semantics outside the task scope."],"risks_b":["Upload also calls Raw.Do directly rather than FilesService.Add, violating a central reuse requirement.","Adds forbidden association options and multipart form-field machinery.","WithFile* option comments claim they associate files uploaded with Add, but Add ignores cfg.form; those options only affect Upload, making the new API misleading."]}
